name: Guidejar
description: Interactive product demos / how-to guides / internal docs — record a process (Chrome or desktop), edit, AI voiceover/translate, share or embed; help-center hosting. Free up to 5 guides; paid unlimited. India-founded, ~10k users claimed.

mentions.evidence: ~$5.0k MRR, 215 active subscriptions, ~$5.5k L30, ~$145k all-time, ~10,000 users claimed, founded Jul 2023, India. Last sync Oct 2, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Capture → shareable guide for one workflow type (onboarding, SOPs, feature tours). Free tier as SEO funnel; seats/workspaces as upgrade.

whyItPrints: Supademo-adjacent documentation infra. Teams buy so support stops screen-sharing the same flow — ~$5k MRR and ~$145k all-time with hundreds of subs.
whyThisMatters:
Teams use Guidejar when the same question keeps showing up. You record the clicks once, in Chrome or in a desktop app for Mac or Windows. It becomes a step-by-step guide or a walkthrough someone can follow alone. Share a link, or embed it.

People use it for internal how-tos, product launches, a demo a prospect can click before a call, onboarding, and sales. You can blur private details, zoom in, add chapters, and branch the path. A writer called Nila rewrites the steps from the screenshots, in your tone, and you can undo that. Add a voiceover, or translate into more than 30 languages while keeping the original. A screen recording turns into numbered steps. Emails, account numbers, and faces can be hidden before you share. Visitors can ask a question and get an answer from the guides. Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok can create and search them through an MCP connection.

Free stops at five guides. Paid use lifts the cap. It started in India in July 2023. They say more than 10,000 people use it. DHL and Pfizer use it too. You record it once so you aren't walking the next person through it.
